evidence.evidence_excerpt: A deliberately failing browser-only test was omitted by the default run, which exited zero.
A later maintainer reproduction got no tests by default and the expected failure with platform chrome.

intended_control: Run a package's test files and make platform-specific exclusions visible when the requested invocation executes none of them.
false_acceptance: The default invocation omitted a browser-only failing test and reported a successful run rather than failing on the empty applicable set.

causal_chain.claim: The test file declares a browser platform and contains an assertion that must fail.
The default invocation omitted that test and returned a successful or no-tests result.
Selecting the Chrome platform executes the test and exposes the assertion failure.
Platform metadata inside the test controls discovery, while the default invocation lacks an external completeness assertion.

steps: Create the issue's test with a browser TestOn annotation and expect(1, 2).
Run the framework test and record the result.
Run the framework test --platform chrome and compare the result.
reproducer.observed: The default run omitted the test; the Chrome run executed it and failed.
reproducer.expected: The default run should not provide a success signal when every supplied test is platform-excluded.

facts: The issue provides a minimal failing test and an exit-zero log.
Maintainer reproduction confirms the platform-dependent discovery boundary.
derivations: The annotation makes the audited test participate in choosing whether it is included.
unknowns: The thread treats explicit platform selection as intended usage and does not settle whether default no-tests success violates a documented contract.
